# 0. Packages and color palette

```{r packages}
# Guarded loader: check availability before library() rather than assuming
# it - consistent with the defensive style already used elsewhere in this
# pipeline (column-name / date-format checks below), extended to packages.
required_pkgs <- c("SpiecEasi", "NetCoMi", "vegan", "ggplot2")
missing_pkgs <- required_pkgs[!vapply(required_pkgs, requireNamespace,
                                       logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
  stop("Required package(s) not installed: ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "),
       ". Install SpiecEasi/NetCoMi from GitHub (zdk123/SpiecEasi, ",
       "stefpeschel/NetCoMi) and vegan/ggplot2 from CRAN before proceeding. ",
       "Not proceeding with an unverified environment.")
}

library(SpiecEasi)   # cross-domain compositional association estimation
library(NetCoMi)     # network construction, analysis, comparison
library(vegan)       # Mantel test, Bray-Curtis dissimilarity
library(ggplot2)      # Section 9c completeness heatmap only
library(patchwork)   # combine per-taxon ggplot2 panels into one figure per lake
library(circlize)

set.seed(123456)      # reproducibility of SpiecEasi/pulsar and clustering

# Colorblind-safe palette (Okabe & Ito 2008) used throughout for node coloring
COL_16S_OTHER <- "#56B4E9"  # blue      = non-cyanobacterial 16S (Bacteria)
COL_CYANO     <- "#D55E00"  # vermilion = Cyanobacteria (16S)
COL_18S       <- "#009E73"  # green     = 18S micro-eukaryotes

# NetCoMi's default edge coloring (green = positive, red = negative) is NOT
# colorblind-safe - red/green is the worst pair for the most common form of
# color blindness. Overridden via NetCoMi's documented posCol/negCol.
COL_EDGE_POS <- "#0072B2"   # blue   = positive association (co-occurrence)
COL_EDGE_NEG <- "#E69F00"   # orange = negative association (mutual exclusion)
```

# 1. Load data

All rows and columns of the uploaded 2023_16S.csv, 2023_18S.csv, and
ossining_meta.csv are read in unmodified here; no subsetting happens until
the explicitly-flagged steps below (organelle/host filtering, per-lake
prevalence filtering), each of which reports exactly what and how much it
removes.

```{r load-data}
counts_16S <- read.csv("results/2023_16S.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
counts_18S <- read.csv("results/2023_18S.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
meta_all   <- read.csv("data/ossining_meta.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)

# Restrict metadata to samples with a matching 2023 sequencing sample.
# (Removes 2022 metadata rows only - does not remove any ASV data.)
meta <- meta_all[meta_all$Year == 2023, ]
meta$SampleShort <- sub("-23$", "", meta$SampleID)   # "LM-6-1-23" -> "LM-6-1"

env_vars_all <- c("Stemp", "Btemp", "SpH", "BpH", "SDO", "BDO", "MC", "NO3", "PO4", "N:P")
lake_lookup  <- c(LM = "Lake Mohegan", LR = "Lake Rippowam", TTL = "Teatown Lake")
```

# 2. Remove non-target (organelle/host) sequences from 16S data

16S universal bacterial/archaeal primers routinely co-amplify chloroplast
and mitochondrial rRNA genes, and can occasionally pick up misclassified
host/eukaryotic sequences. Removing these prior to analysis is standard
practice for 16S community data (see e.g. the QIIME2/DADA2 taxonomy-based
filtering tutorials; Bokulich et al. 2018, *mSystems*). This runs before
Section 3's Taxa-level aggregation and Cyanobacteria detection, because
chloroplasts are phylogenetically nested within Cyanobacteria in most
reference taxonomies (SILVA, GTDB) and typically labeled `Phylum =
Cyanobacteriota, Class = Chloroplast` -- if not removed first, chloroplast
reads would be miscounted as genuine Cyanobacteria in Section 3.

Filter criteria: `Class == "Chloroplast"`, `Family == "Mitochondria"`,
`Kingdom == "Eukaryota"`.

```{r organelle-filter}
# Confirm required columns exist before filtering - do not assume they do
required_cols <- c("Class", "Family", "Kingdom")
missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(counts_16S))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop("2023_16S.csv is missing required column(s) for organelle/host filtering: ",
       paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
       ". Not proceeding until columns are confirmed present.")
}

# NA-safe: NA in Class/Family/Kingdom is treated as "not matching" rather
# than propagating NA into the logical index
is_chloroplast  <- !is.na(counts_16S$Class)   & counts_16S$Class   == "Chloroplast"
is_mitochondria <- !is.na(counts_16S$Family)  & counts_16S$Family  == "Mitochondria"
is_eukaryota    <- !is.na(counts_16S$Kingdom) & counts_16S$Kingdom == "Eukaryota"
remove_idx <- is_chloroplast | is_mitochondria | is_eukaryota

sample_cols_16S_raw <- grep("^16S-", names(counts_16S), value = TRUE)
n_asv_removed   <- sum(remove_idx)
n_reads_removed <- sum(as.matrix(counts_16S[remove_idx, sample_cols_16S_raw, drop = FALSE]))
n_reads_total   <- sum(as.matrix(counts_16S[, sample_cols_16S_raw, drop = FALSE]))

cat("\n=== 16S organelle/host sequence filtering ===\n")
cat("ASVs removed - Chloroplast (Class):", sum(is_chloroplast), "\n")
cat("ASVs removed - Mitochondria (Family):", sum(is_mitochondria), "\n")
cat("ASVs removed - Eukaryota (Kingdom):", sum(is_eukaryota), "\n")
cat("Total ASVs removed:", n_asv_removed, "of", nrow(counts_16S),
    "(", round(100 * n_asv_removed / nrow(counts_16S), 1), "%)\n")
cat("Total reads removed:", n_reads_removed, "of", n_reads_total,
    "(", round(100 * n_reads_removed / n_reads_total, 1), "%)\n")

# Full audit trail - nothing discarded without a record of exactly what/why
write.csv(counts_16S[remove_idx, ],
          "results/16S_removed_chloroplast_mitochondria_eukaryota.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Apply the filter - all downstream 16S steps use this filtered object
counts_16S <- counts_16S[!remove_idx, ]
```

# 3. Aggregate ASV counts to the "Taxa" column; identify Cyanobacteria and HAB genera

```{r aggregate-taxa}
aggregate_to_taxa <- function(df, sample_cols, taxa_col, higher_col) {
  taxa_label <- df[[taxa_col]]
  taxa_label[is.na(taxa_label) | taxa_label %in% c("NA", "")] <- "Unclassified"
  count_mat <- as.matrix(df[, sample_cols])
  agg <- rowsum(count_mat, group = taxa_label)   # sum ASV counts within each Taxa label

  # Most common higher-rank label per Taxa entry, for node coloring /
  # Cyanobacteria identification
  higher_lookup <- tapply(df[[higher_col]], taxa_label,
                           function(x) names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1])
  list(counts = agg, higher = higher_lookup[rownames(agg)])
}

sample_cols_16S <- grep("^16S-", names(counts_16S), value = TRUE)
sample_cols_18S <- grep("^18S-", names(counts_18S), value = TRUE)

taxa_16S <- aggregate_to_taxa(counts_16S, sample_cols_16S, "Taxa", "Phylum")
taxa_18S <- aggregate_to_taxa(counts_18S, sample_cols_18S, "Taxa", "Division")

# This data set labels the cyanobacterial phylum "Cyanobacteriota" (GTDB-style
# nomenclature), not "Cyanobacteria" - verified directly in the data (do not
# assume nomenclature; confirm it in the object being used).
cyano_taxa <- rownames(taxa_16S$counts)[taxa_16S$higher == "Cyanobacteriota"]
cat("Cyanobacteria taxa detected (16S, Phylum = 'Cyanobacteriota'):\n")
print(cyano_taxa)
```

```{r hab-list}
# User-specified HAB-forming (harmful algal bloom) genera. This list is
# NOT cross-checked against external nomenclature databases, and - as
# flagged below - is not guaranteed to be a subset of cyano_taxa above,
# which matters for the Section 9 completeness-matrix fix (stage 3a).
HAB_TAXA <- c("Aliinostoc", "Aphanizomenon", "Cephalothrix", "Chrysosporum",
              "Cuspidothrix", "Cyanobium", "Desikacharya", "Dolichospermum",
              "Geitlerinema", "Lacustricoccus", "Leptolyngbya", "Limnococcus",
              "Limnothrix", "Marileptolyngbya", "Microcystis", "Nodosilinea",
              "Planktothrix", "Pseudoanabaena", "Radiocystis", "Raphidiopsis",
              "Regnicoccus", "Vulcanococcus", "Woronichinia")

HAB_detected <- intersect(HAB_TAXA, rownames(taxa_16S$counts))
HAB_absent   <- setdiff(HAB_TAXA, rownames(taxa_16S$counts))

# FIXED (Rmd review, bug #2 setup): explicitly report which detected HAB
# genera are NOT labeled Phylum = Cyanobacteriota in this taxonomy, since
# those genera will be silently excluded from Section 7's correlation
# testing set - this warning makes that fact visible up front rather than
# only showing up as an unexplained gap in Section 9.
HAB_detected_not_cyano <- setdiff(HAB_detected, cyano_taxa)
if (length(HAB_detected_not_cyano) > 0) {
  message("HAB-list genera detected in the data but NOT labeled Phylum = ",
          "'Cyanobacteriota' in this taxonomy (will be excluded from Section 7's ",
          "environmental-correlation testing set, and flagged as stage 3a rather ",
          "than stage 3 in Section 9): ", paste(HAB_detected_not_cyano, collapse = ", "))
}

cat("\nUser-specified HAB-forming genera FOUND in 'Taxa' column of 2023_16S.csv ",
    "(pooled across all lakes, before prevalence filtering):\n")
print(HAB_detected)
if (length(HAB_absent) > 0) {
  message("HAB-list genera NOT found anywhere in this dataset's 'Taxa' column ",
          "(absent from these lakes/samples, or spelled/classified differently ",
          "in this taxonomy - not verified against external nomenclature): ",
          paste(HAB_absent, collapse = ", "))
}
```

# 4. Per-lake data prep: sample matching, prevalence filtering

```{r prevalence-filter}
min_prevalence <- 0.20   # ADJUSTABLE - not a universal standard (see Results outline 5.3)

filter_prevalence <- function(mat, min_frac) {
  n <- ncol(mat)
  min_samp <- ceiling(min_frac * n)
  keep <- rowSums(mat > 0) >= min_samp
  mat[keep, , drop = FALSE]
}

lake_data <- list()

for (code in names(lake_lookup)) {

  samp16 <- grep(paste0("^16S-", code, "-"), sample_cols_16S, value = TRUE)
  samp18 <- grep(paste0("^18S-", code, "-"), sample_cols_18S, value = TRUE)
  short16 <- sub("^16S-", "", samp16)
  short18 <- sub("^18S-", "", samp18)

  common <- Reduce(intersect, list(short16, short18,
                                    meta$SampleShort[meta$Lake == lake_lookup[code]]))
  common <- sort(common)

  m16 <- taxa_16S$counts[, paste0("16S-", common), drop = FALSE]
  m18 <- taxa_18S$counts[, paste0("18S-", common), drop = FALSE]

  m16_filt <- filter_prevalence(m16, min_prevalence)
  m18_filt <- filter_prevalence(m18, min_prevalence)

  dropped_cyano <- setdiff(cyano_taxa, rownames(m16_filt))
  if (length(dropped_cyano) > 0) {
    message("Lake ", code, ": Cyanobacteria taxa removed by the ", min_prevalence * 100,
            "% prevalence filter (present in too few samples): ",
            paste(dropped_cyano, collapse = ", "))
  }

  lake_data[[code]] <- list(samples = common, m16 = m16_filt, m18 = m18_filt)

  cat("Lake", code, "-", length(common), "paired 16S/18S samples;",
      nrow(m16_filt), "16S taxa and", nrow(m18_filt), "18S taxa retained\n")
}
```

# 5. Cross-domain network per lake (SpiecEasi -> NetCoMi)

Parameters and function calls below (`multi.spiec.easi`, `symBeta`,
`getOptBeta`, `getOptInd`, `getRefit`, `getStability`, `netConstruct`,
`netAnalyze`) match NetCoMi's own documented cross-domain-networks vignette
and SpiecEasi's cross-domain vignette usage.

```{r networks}
# =====================================================================
# Section 5 replacement: "Cross-domain network per lake (SpiecEasi ->
# NetCoMi)". Only the PLOTTING block at the end changes (everything above
# it - multi.spiec.easi fitting, StARS boundary diagnostics, netConstruct/
# netAnalyze, lake_results assembly - is UNCHANGED from the original).
#
# CHANGES:
#   - Node labels are now numbers (1..N per lake, alphabetical), passed
#     via plot.microNetProps()'s documented `labels` argument (a named
#     character vector keyed to the adjacency matrix's row/column names -
#     confirmed in NetCoMi's own reference docs, not assumed) instead of
#     the taxon names or the previous "hide labels via cexLabels~0"
#     workaround.
#   - The plot is now saved as an SVG (it previously was not saved to
#     disk at all - only rendered inline in the knitted document).
#   - A per-node lookup table is exported per lake and combined across
#     lakes: Number, Taxon, Domain, is_HAB, raw edge count (Degree),
#     mean/max |asso| across that taxon's own edges, NetCoMi's own
#     centrality measures (degree/betweenness/closeness/eigenvector), and
#     hub-taxon status (props$hubs, via the same get_hub_taxa() extraction
#     pattern used in Section 7 v3 - duplicated here since Section 5 runs
#     BEFORE Section 7 in this Rmd and cannot depend on it having already
#     defined that helper).
# =====================================================================

# Duplicated from Section 7 v3 (see that chunk's comment) - kept identical
# in both places intentionally, so Section 5 doesn't depend on chunk
# execution order. If you consolidate this into a single shared setup
# chunk later, remove one of the two copies, not both independently.
get_hub_taxa <- function(props) {
  hubs <- props$hubs
  hub_names <- if (!is.null(hubs$hubs1)) hubs$hubs1 else hubs   # verify against str(props$hubs) if this ever errors
  as.character(hub_names)
}

lake_results <- list()
full_network_tables <- list()

for (code in names(lake_data)) {

  d <- lake_data[[code]]

  m16_t <- t(d$m16)
  m18_t <- t(d$m18)
  rownames(m16_t) <- d$samples
  rownames(m18_t) <- d$samples
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(m16_t), rownames(m18_t)))

  nlambda_val <- 30
  lambda_min_ratio_val <- 1e-2

  se_fit <- SpiecEasi::multi.spiec.easi(
    list(m16_t, m18_t),
    method = "mb",
    nlambda = nlambda_val,
    lambda.min.ratio = lambda_min_ratio_val,
    pulsar.params = list(thresh = 0.05, rep.num = 50)
  )

  assoMat <- as.matrix(SpiecEasi::symBeta(SpiecEasi::getOptBeta(se_fit), mode = "ave"))
  taxa_names <- c(rownames(d$m16), rownames(d$m18))
  colnames(assoMat) <- rownames(assoMat) <- taxa_names
  diag(assoMat) <- 1

  opt_idx <- SpiecEasi::getOptInd(se_fit)
  at_boundary <- opt_idx %in% c(1, nlambda_val)
  n_edges <- sum(as.matrix(SpiecEasi::getRefit(se_fit))) / 2
  n_possible <- choose(length(taxa_names), 2)
  cat("\nLake", code, "- network diagnostics:\n")
  cat("  Taxa (nodes):", length(taxa_names), "| Samples:", nrow(m16_t), "\n")
  cat("  Edges:", n_edges, "/", n_possible, "possible (density =",
      round(n_edges / n_possible, 3), ")\n")
  cat("  StARS stability at selected lambda:", round(SpiecEasi::getStability(se_fit), 3),
      "(target = pulsar.params$thresh = 0.05)\n")
  if (at_boundary) {
    warning("Lake ", code, ": StARS selected the lambda path BOUNDARY (index ", opt_idx,
            " of ", nlambda_val, "). Widen the path (increase nlambda / decrease ",
            "lambda.min.ratio) and re-run before trusting this network's density.")
  }

  net   <- NetCoMi::netConstruct(data = assoMat, dataType = "condDependence", sparsMethod = "none")
  props <- NetCoMi::netAnalyze(net, hubPar = "eigenvector", clustMethod = "cluster_fast_greedy")

  edge_w <- abs(net$edgelist1$asso)
  cat("  Edge-weight (|association|) distribution, n =", length(edge_w), "edges:\n")
  print(round(quantile(edge_w, probs = c(0, .25, .5, .75, .9, .95, 1)), 3))

  domain_vec <- setNames(c(rep("16S", nrow(d$m16)), rep("18S", nrow(d$m18))), taxa_names)
  is_cyano <- taxa_names %in% cyano_taxa
  nodeCols <- setNames(
    ifelse(is_cyano, COL_CYANO, ifelse(domain_vec == "16S", COL_16S_OTHER, COL_18S)),
    taxa_names
  )

  lake_results[[code]] <- list(assoMat = assoMat, taxa = taxa_names, domain = domain_vec,
                                net = net, props = props, nodeCols = nodeCols, edge_w = edge_w,
                                m16 = d$m16, m18 = d$m18, samples = d$samples)

  # ---- Number labels: alphabetical, 1..N, keyed to taxa_names so the
  # named vector's names match assoMat's row/column names exactly, as
  # plot.microNetProps()'s `labels` argument requires. ----
  node_number <- setNames(seq_along(sort(taxa_names)), sort(taxa_names))
  label_vec <- setNames(as.character(node_number[taxa_names]), taxa_names)

  render_full_network_plot <- function() {
    plot(props, nodeColor = "colorVec", colorVec = nodeCols,
         nodeSize = "eigenvector", nodeSizeSpread = 3,
         labels = label_vec, labelScale = FALSE, cexLabels = 0.01,
         rmSingles = "all", edgeFilter = "none",
         posCol = COL_EDGE_POS, negCol = COL_EDGE_NEG,
         title1 = lake_lookup[code], showTitle = TRUE, cexTitle = 1.4)
    legend(-1.6, -1.1, cex = 0.7, pt.cex = 1.3,
           legend = c("Other Bacteria (16S)", "Cyanobacteria (16S)", "Micro-eukaryotes (18S)",
                      "+ association", "- association"),
           col = c(COL_16S_OTHER, COL_CYANO, COL_18S, COL_EDGE_POS, COL_EDGE_NEG),
           pch = c(16, 16, 16, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, NA, NA, 1, 1), lwd = 2, bty = "n", xpd = TRUE)
  }

  svg(paste0("results/full_network_", code, ".svg"), width = 12, height = 10)
  render_full_network_plot()
  dev.off()

  render_full_network_plot()   # on-screen / knitted-document copy

  # ---- Per-node lookup table: number, taxonomy, degree, association
  # summary, centrality, and hub status. ----
  edges <- net$edgelist1
  cent  <- props$centralities
  hub_taxa_lake <- get_hub_taxa(props)

  node_stats <- lapply(taxa_names, function(tx) {
    touch <- edges$v1 == tx | edges$v2 == tx
    n_edge <- sum(touch)
    abs_asso_tx <- abs(edges$asso[touch])
    data.frame(
      Lake = lake_lookup[code],
      Number = node_number[[tx]],
      Taxon = tx,
      Domain = domain_vec[[tx]],
      is_HAB = tx %in% HAB_TAXA,
      is_hub_taxon = tx %in% hub_taxa_lake,
      Degree = n_edge,
      Plotted_in_figure = n_edge > 0,   # rmSingles = "all" drops degree-0 nodes from the SVG
      Mean_abs_asso = if (n_edge > 0) mean(abs_asso_tx) else NA_real_,
      Max_abs_asso  = if (n_edge > 0) max(abs_asso_tx)  else NA_real_,
      Degree_centrality_norm      = unname(cent$degree1[tx]),
      Betweenness_centrality_norm = unname(cent$between1[tx]),
      Closeness_centrality_norm   = unname(cent$close1[tx]),
      Eigenvector_centrality_norm = unname(cent$eigenv1[tx]),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  full_network_tables[[code]] <- do.call(rbind, node_stats)

  write.csv(full_network_tables[[code]][order(full_network_tables[[code]]$Number), ],
            paste0("results/full_network_taxon_reference_", code, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

full_network_table_all <- do.call(rbind, full_network_tables)
full_network_table_all <- full_network_table_all[order(full_network_table_all$Lake,
                                                          full_network_table_all$Number), ]
write.csv(full_network_table_all, "results/full_network_taxon_reference_all_lakes.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n=== Full-network per-node reference table, all lakes (also written to CSV) ===\n")
print(head(full_network_table_all, 20))
```

# 6. Cyanobacteria-centered edge extraction (biotic co-occurrence)

```{r cyano-edges}
cyano_edge_summary <- list()

for (code in names(lake_results)) {
  r <- lake_results[[code]]
  edges <- r$net$edgelist1   # columns: v1, v2, asso (netConstruct() docs)

  cyano_edges <- edges[edges$v1 %in% cyano_taxa | edges$v2 %in% cyano_taxa, ]
  cyano_edges$partner_domain <- ifelse(cyano_edges$v1 %in% cyano_taxa,
                                        r$domain[cyano_edges$v2], r$domain[cyano_edges$v1])
  cyano_edges$is_HAB <- (cyano_edges$v1 %in% HAB_TAXA) | (cyano_edges$v2 %in% HAB_TAXA)
  cyano_edges$lake <- lake_lookup[code]
  cyano_edge_summary[[code]] <- cyano_edges

  cat("\nLake", code, "- Cyanobacteria co-occurrence edges:", nrow(cyano_edges),
      "( to 18S partners:", sum(cyano_edges$partner_domain == "18S"),
      "; involving HAB-list genera:", sum(cyano_edges$is_HAB), ")\n")
}

cyano_edges_all <- do.call(rbind, cyano_edge_summary)
write.csv(cyano_edges_all, "results/cyanobacteria_cooccurrence_edges_by_lake.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# HAB-specific edges, strongest |association| first
hab_edges_all <- cyano_edges_all[cyano_edges_all$is_HAB, ]
hab_edges_all <- hab_edges_all[order(-abs(hab_edges_all$asso)), ]
cat("\n=== HAB-list genus co-occurrence edges (all lakes, strongest first) ===\n")
print(head(hab_edges_all, 20))
```

```{r rank hab}
# =====================================================================
# 7a. Rank HAB genera by abundance within Cyanobacteria (matches Figure 6)
#
# ADDED - previously referenced by Section 8/8a ("top_hab_by_abundance",
# "TOP_N_ABUNDANT") but never defined anywhere in this Rmd, which is what
# produced "Error: object 'top_hab_by_abundance' not found".
#
# Per confirmed definition:
#   - Abundance basis: each genus's reads / TOTAL CYANOBACTERIA reads in
#     that sample (relative abundance WITHIN Cyanobacteria, not within
#     total 16S or total 16S+18S community) - matches how Figure 6 is
#     described as being constructed (2023_16S_ReAnalyzed_Diversity.Rmd).
#   - Ranking pool: HAB_TAXA genera that are ALSO classified Cyanobacteriota
#     in this taxonomy (cyano_taxa) - a HAB-list genus not in cyano_taxa
#     has no defined "% of Cyanobacteria reads" (already flagged separately
#     as HAB_detected_not_cyano in Section 3).
#   - TOP_N_ABUNDANT = 5, per confirmation.
#   - Uses lake_data[[code]]$m16 - the POST-prevalence-filter matrix
#     (Section 4), i.e. the same filtered counts every other per-lake step
#     in this pipeline uses, not the unfiltered taxa_16S$counts.
# =====================================================================

TOP_N_ABUNDANT <- 5   # top N HAB genera per lake, by mean %-of-Cyanobacteria abundance

top_hab_by_abundance <- list()

for (code in names(lake_data)) {
  m16 <- lake_data[[code]]$m16
  cyano_in_lake     <- intersect(cyano_taxa, rownames(m16))
  hab_cyano_in_lake <- intersect(HAB_TAXA, cyano_in_lake)

  if (length(cyano_in_lake) == 0 || length(hab_cyano_in_lake) == 0) {
    message("Lake ", code, ": no HAB-list genera classified as Cyanobacteriota and present ",
            "after prevalence filtering - top_hab_by_abundance[['", code, "']] set to ",
            "character(0), so Section 8/8a will skip this lake rather than error.")
    top_hab_by_abundance[[code]] <- character(0)
    next
  }

  # Relative abundance WITHIN Cyanobacteria: genus reads / total
  # Cyanobacteria reads, per sample (NOT total 16S, NOT total community).
  cyano_counts <- m16[cyano_in_lake, , drop = FALSE]
  cyano_totals_per_sample <- colSums(cyano_counts)

  if (any(cyano_totals_per_sample == 0)) {
    zero_samples <- names(cyano_totals_per_sample)[cyano_totals_per_sample == 0]
    message("Lake ", code, ": sample(s) with ZERO total Cyanobacteria reads after ",
            "prevalence filtering (", paste(zero_samples, collapse = ", "), ") - excluded from ",
            "this lake's mean relative-abundance calculation to avoid division by zero.")
  }
  valid_samples <- names(cyano_totals_per_sample)[cyano_totals_per_sample > 0]

  cyano_rel_within <- sweep(cyano_counts[, valid_samples, drop = FALSE], 2,
                            cyano_totals_per_sample[valid_samples], "/")

  mean_rel_abund <- rowMeans(cyano_rel_within[hab_cyano_in_lake, , drop = FALSE])
  ranked <- sort(mean_rel_abund, decreasing = TRUE)

  n_take <- min(TOP_N_ABUNDANT, length(ranked))
  if (n_take < TOP_N_ABUNDANT) {
    message("Lake ", code, ": only ", n_take, " HAB-list Cyanobacteria genus/genera available ",
            "(fewer than TOP_N_ABUNDANT = ", TOP_N_ABUNDANT, ") - using all of them.")
  }
  top_hab_by_abundance[[code]] <- names(ranked)[seq_len(n_take)]

  cat("Lake", code, "- top", n_take, "HAB genera by mean % of Cyanobacteria reads:\n")
  print(round(ranked[seq_len(n_take)] * 100, 2))
}
```
