```{r hab-subnetwork}
# =====================================================================
# Section 7 replacement chunk, v3: `{r hab-subnetwork}`
# CHANGED (per user request): node colors now match the diversity-analysis
# bar plots (Figures 5-7) instead of the 3-way domain scheme (16S-other /
# Cyanobacteria / 18S). Specifically:
#   - 16S non-cyanobacteria nodes -> colored by Phylum (Figure 5's palette)
#   - Cyanobacteria nodes         -> colored by Taxa/genus (Figure 6's palette)
#   - 18S nodes                   -> colored by Taxa2 (Figure 7's palette)
# A legend is added to the right of each circos plot listing every node
# actually plotted, colored to match, with "(Phylum)"/"(Taxa2)" appended
# to 16S/18S node names and cyanobacteria nodes left as their bare Taxa
# name (per request - the color IS the taxon-level identifier for those).
#
# REQUIRES: PHYLUM_COLORS_16S, CYANO_TAXA_COLORS_16S, and
# DIVISION_COLORS_18S_TAXA2 (color_lookup_tables.R) loaded before this chunk.
# =====================================================================

# ---- Load the three color lookup tables (see color_lookup_tables.R) ----
# source("color_lookup_tables.R")   # UNCOMMENT once that file is in the same project

# ---- Verify counts_18S carries the SAME 'Taxa2' column that produced
# Figure 7 (NOT 'Division' - see explanation in color_lookup_tables.R
# header). Fails loudly rather than silently falling back to the coarser
# 'Division' field, which would give WRONG colors for every Opisthokonta_*
# subgroup (they'd all collapse to whatever single color 'Opisthokonta'
# happens to get under Division).
if (!("Taxa2" %in% names(counts_18S))) {
  stop("counts_18S (2023_18S.csv) has no 'Taxa2' column. Figure 7's colors are keyed to ",
       "'Taxa2' (2023_18S_ReAnalyzed_Diversity.Rmd), which the diversity pipeline describes ",
       "as an edited/finer version of 'Division' - NOT the same field currently used in ",
       "Section 3 (aggregate_to_taxa(..., higher_col = \"Division\")). Add a 'Taxa2' column ",
       "to 2023_18S.csv from the same source used in the diversity Rmd before proceeding - ",
       "not falling back to 'Division' automatically, since that would silently produce ",
       "colors that don't match Figure 7 for every Opisthokonta_* subgroup.")
}

# ---- Build a Taxa -> Taxa2 lookup (most common Taxa2 per aggregated Taxa
# label), the same pattern aggregate_to_taxa() already uses for Division/
# Phylum in Section 3 - added here as a second higher-rank lookup specific
# to 18S, without altering Section 3's existing taxa_18S$higher (Division),
# which other parts of the pipeline may still depend on.
taxa2_lookup <- tapply(counts_18S$Taxa2, counts_18S$Taxa,
                       function(x) names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1])

#' Extract a scalar character value from a tapply()-built lookup vector.
#' tapply() silently falls back to storing its result as a LIST-mode array
#' (rather than a plain atomic vector) whenever its per-group function
#' doesn't return a perfectly uniform scalar across every group - confirmed
#' to be the actual case here for taxa_16S$higher (built in Section 3 of
#' the interdomain Rmd) and taxa2_lookup (built above). In that mode,
#' single-bracket `lookup_vec[key]` returns a one-element LIST instead of
#' a bare string, which then fails with "invalid subscript type 'list'"
#' if used directly as a subscript elsewhere - unlist() here flattens
#' either representation (plain atomic OR list-mode) to a bare character
#' value, and returns NA_character_ (never an error) if key isn't found.
safe_lookup <- function(lookup_vec, key) {
  raw <- lookup_vec[key]
  val <- unlist(raw, use.names = FALSE)
  if (length(val) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  as.character(val)[1]
}

#' Resolve a node's plot color and legend label.
#' - Cyanobacteria (in cyano_taxa): color from CYANO_TAXA_COLORS_16S, label = bare Taxa name.
#' - 16S non-cyano: color from PHYLUM_COLORS_16S via taxa_16S$higher (Phylum), label = "Taxon (Phylum)".
#' - 18S: color from DIVISION_COLORS_18S_TAXA2 via taxa2_lookup, label = "Taxon (Taxa2)".
#' Never guesses: any taxon whose phylum/Taxa2 isn't in the corresponding
#' color table gets FALLBACK_COLOR and is reported by name so it can be
#' checked, rather than silently mis-colored.
#'
#' NOTE: PHYLUM_COLORS_16S / CYANO_TAXA_COLORS_16S / DIVISION_COLORS_18S_TAXA2
#' are plain atomic vectors (built with c(...) in color_lookup_tables.R), so
#' `[name]` + is.na() is safe for those. taxa_16S$higher and taxa2_lookup are
#' tapply()-built and go through safe_lookup() instead - see its comment.
FALLBACK_COLOR <- "grey60"

resolve_node_color <- function(taxon, domain) {
  if (taxon %in% cyano_taxa) {
    col <- unname(CYANO_TAXA_COLORS_16S[taxon])
    if (is.na(col)) {
      message("No Figure-6 color for cyanobacteria taxon '", taxon, "' (likely below the ",
              "diversity pipeline's 1%-abundance filter for that figure, despite passing this ",
              "network's 20%-prevalence filter) - using fallback color.")
      return(list(color = FALLBACK_COLOR, label = taxon))
    }
    return(list(color = col, label = taxon))
  }
  if (domain == "16S") {
    phylum <- safe_lookup(taxa_16S$higher, taxon)
    if (is.na(phylum)) {
      message("No Phylum recorded for taxon '", taxon, "' in taxa_16S$higher - using fallback color.")
      return(list(color = FALLBACK_COLOR, label = paste0(taxon, " (Unclassified)")))
    }
    col <- unname(PHYLUM_COLORS_16S[phylum])
    if (is.na(col)) {
      message("No Figure-5 color for phylum '", phylum, "' (taxon '", taxon, "') - ",
              "using fallback color. Check whether this phylum was present in the diversity ",
              "pipeline's 2023 16S dataset (Figure 5's source).")
      return(list(color = FALLBACK_COLOR, label = paste0(taxon, " (", phylum, ")")))
    }
    return(list(color = col, label = paste0(taxon, " (", phylum, ")")))
  }
  # 18S
  tx2 <- safe_lookup(taxa2_lookup, taxon)
  if (is.na(tx2)) {
    message("No Taxa2 recorded for taxon '", taxon, "' in taxa2_lookup - using fallback color.")
    return(list(color = FALLBACK_COLOR, label = paste0(taxon, " (Unclassified)")))
  }
  col <- unname(DIVISION_COLORS_18S_TAXA2[tx2])
  if (is.na(col)) {
    message("No Figure-7 color for Taxa2 '", tx2, "' (taxon '", taxon, "') - ",
            "using fallback color. Check whether this Taxa2 category was present in the ",
            "diversity pipeline's 2023 18S dataset (Figure 7's source).")
    return(list(color = FALLBACK_COLOR, label = paste0(taxon, " (", tx2, ")")))
  }
  list(color = col, label = paste0(taxon, " (", tx2, ")"))
}

neighbor_tables <- list()

cat("Checking centrality structure for first lake (verify before trusting extraction):\n")
str(lake_results[[1]]$props$centralities)

TOP_N_PARTNERS <- 5   # ADJUSTABLE - number of strongest direct partners kept per HAB taxon

LABEL_CEX_HAB    <- 0.8    # HAB-list anchor genera - larger, bold-ish (font=4)
LABEL_CEX_PARTNER <- 0.55  # partner taxa - smaller, italic (font=3)
LABEL_FONT_HAB    <- 4
LABEL_FONT_PARTNER<- 3

#' Return the top-N direct partners of one taxon by |asso|, from a lake's
#' full edgelist. Never recomputes asso - reads directly from
#' r$net$edgelist1, the same object Section 8's tornado plots use, so the
#' ranking here always matches what's shown there.
get_top_n_partners <- function(edges, taxon, n) {
  touch <- edges$v1 == taxon | edges$v2 == taxon
  sub <- edges[touch, ]
  if (nrow(sub) == 0) return(character(0))
  sub$partner <- ifelse(sub$v1 == taxon, sub$v2, sub$v1)
  sub <- sub[order(-abs(sub$asso)), ]
  head(sub$partner, n)
}

# CHANGED: hab_present and partner_taxa are computed ONCE per lake (in the
# render loop below) and passed in. node_colors/node_labels (named
# color/label per taxon, from resolve_node_color()) are also computed
# once per lake and passed in, so the plotted nodes and the legend can
# never disagree.
plot_hab_subnetwork_circlize <- function(code, neighbor_set, hab_present, partner_taxa,
                                          node_colors, node_labels) {
  r <- lake_results[[code]]
  edges_all <- r$net$edgelist1
  edges <- edges_all[edges_all$v1 %in% neighbor_set & edges_all$v2 %in% neighbor_set, ]
  node_order <- sort(neighbor_set)

  # CHANGED (per request): the ring shows a NUMBER per node instead of the
  # full taxon name - numbers are keyed to the right-side legend below, so
  # the plot stays compact and readable even with 50-80 nodes. Numbering
  # is 1..N in node_order (alphabetical), computed HERE from neighbor_set
  # alone, so the ring and the legend always agree - it is never passed in
  # separately, which would risk drifting out of sync if node_order's
  # sort ever changed upstream.
  node_number <- setNames(seq_along(node_order), node_order)

  cent <- r$props$centralities
  eig_vals <- tryCatch({
    v <- cent$eigenv1[node_order]
    if (any(is.na(v))) stop("NA after matching")
    v
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  node_cex <- if (is.null(eig_vals)) {
    warning("Lake ", code, ": could not extract eigenvector centrality - using uniform size.")
    setNames(rep(1, length(node_order)), node_order)
  } else {
    rng <- range(eig_vals)
    if (diff(rng) > 0) setNames(0.5 + 1.5 * (eig_vals - rng[1]) / diff(rng), node_order)
    else setNames(rep(1, length(node_order)), node_order)
  }
  # CHANGED: node_col now comes from resolve_node_color() (per-taxon,
  # matched to Figures 5-7), not r$nodeCols (the old 3-way domain scheme).
  node_col <- node_colors[node_order]

  w_rng <- range(abs(edges$asso))
  edge_lwd <- if (diff(w_rng) > 0) 0.3 + 3 * (abs(edges$asso) - w_rng[1]) / diff(w_rng)
              else rep(1, nrow(edges))
  edge_col <- ifelse(edges$asso >= 0, COL_EDGE_POS, COL_EDGE_NEG)

  # CHANGED (per request): the circle and the legend now live in two
  # SEPARATE layout() panels, side by side. Previously the legend was
  # drawn at data-coordinate x = 1.65, in the SAME coordinate system as
  # the circle itself (canvas.xlim/ylim = c(-1.5, 1.5)) - but circlize
  # keeps that coordinate system aspect-locked 1:1 so the circle doesn't
  # stretch into an ellipse. On a wide device, that lock means most of
  # the extra width outside the circle is empty margin the plotting
  # coordinates can't actually reach - widening the device didn't give
  # the legend more usable room, just more invisible margin. A separate
  # layout() panel has its own genuine width, independent of the circle's
  # aspect lock, so a 3rd (or 4th) legend column reliably stays on-canvas.
  # LAYOUT_WIDTHS is the circos-panel : legend-panel width ratio - widen
  # the second number if columns are still tight once you see it rendered.
  LAYOUT_WIDTHS <- c(0.58, 0.42)
  layout(matrix(c(1, 2), nrow = 1), widths = LAYOUT_WIDTHS)

  # ---- Panel 1: circos plot only (no legend drawn in this panel) ----
  circos.clear()
  circos.par(start.degree = 90, clock.wise = TRUE, gap.degree = 1,
             cell.padding = c(0, 0, 0, 0), track.margin = c(0.005, 0.005),
             canvas.xlim = c(-1.3, 1.3), canvas.ylim = c(-1.3, 1.3))
  circos.initialize(sectors = node_order, xlim = c(0, 1))

  # CHANGED (per request): track creation order swapped so numbers sit
  # OUTSIDE the point markers, not inside. circlize places each new
  # circos.track() just INSIDE the previously created one - so whichever
  # track is created first ends up outermost. Previously points were
  # created first (outermost) and numbers second (nested inside them);
  # now numbers are created first (track.index = 1, outermost) and points
  # second (track.index = 2, just inside the numbers ring).
  circos.track(ylim = c(0, 1), track.height = mm_h(6), bg.border = NA,
               panel.fun = function(x, y) {
                 sec <- CELL_META$sector.index
                 is_hab <- sec %in% hab_present
                 circos.text(0.5, 0.2, labels = as.character(node_number[sec]),
                             facing = "clockwise", niceFacing = TRUE,
                             adj = c(0, 0.5),
                             cex  = if (is_hab) LABEL_CEX_HAB else LABEL_CEX_PARTNER,
                             font = if (is_hab) LABEL_FONT_HAB else LABEL_FONT_PARTNER)
               })

  circos.track(ylim = c(0, 1), track.height = mm_h(4), bg.border = NA,
               panel.fun = function(x, y) {
                 sec <- CELL_META$sector.index
                 circos.points(0.5, 0.5, pch = 16, cex = node_cex[sec], col = node_col[sec])
               })

  # circos.link()'s default attachment radius is "just inside the most
  # recently created track" - calling it here (after the points track,
  # now the innermost one) keeps links attaching right at the points,
  # exactly as before; only the points track's radial position changed,
  # not where links attach relative to it.
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(edges))) {
    circos.link(edges$v1[i], 0.5, edges$v2[i], 0.5, col = edge_col[i], lwd = edge_lwd[i])
  }

  # Outline circle marking the HAB-anchor nodes specifically. track.index
  # updated to 2 (points track's new index, since numbers are now
  # track.index 1) - this MUST match wherever the points track actually
  # is, or the black outline circles would be drawn at the wrong radius.
  hab_polar <- t(sapply(hab_present, function(nm) circlize(0.5, 0.5, sector.index = nm, track.index = 2)))
  colnames(hab_polar) <- c("theta", "rou")
  hab_x <- hab_polar[, "rou"] * cos(hab_polar[, "theta"] * pi / 180)
  hab_y <- hab_polar[, "rou"] * sin(hab_polar[, "theta"] * pi / 180)
  points(hab_x, hab_y, pch = 21, cex = node_cex[hab_present] * 1.15,
         col = "black", bg = NA, lwd = 1.2)

  title(paste0(lake_lookup[code], " - HAB genera + top ", TOP_N_PARTNERS, " partners each"), cex.main = 1.1)

  legend("bottom", inset = -0.02, horiz = TRUE, cex = 0.55, pt.cex = 1.1, xpd = NA,
         legend = c("+ association", "- association"),
         col = c(COL_EDGE_POS, COL_EDGE_NEG),
         lty = c(1, 1), lwd = 2, bty = "n")

  circos.clear()

  # ---- Panel 2: legend only, in its own plain (non-aspect-locked) plot
  # region, sized by LAYOUT_WIDTHS[2] above - this is what makes every
  # column genuinely fit rather than running off the device. ----
  par(mar = c(1, 0.5, 1, 0.5))
  plot.new()

  # ROWS_PER_LEGEND_COL controls column-wrapping; LEGEND_CEX controls text
  # size - adjustable together if a given lake's node count still doesn't
  # fit comfortably: fewer rows-per-column -> more, narrower columns
  # (needs more of LAYOUT_WIDTHS[2]); more rows-per-column -> fewer,
  # wider columns (needs more device height instead).
  ROWS_PER_LEGEND_COL <- 26
  LEGEND_CEX <- 0.55
  numbered_labels <- paste0(node_number[node_order], ". ", node_labels[node_order])
  legend("topleft", xpd = NA,
         legend = numbered_labels, pch = 16, col = node_col,
         cex = LEGEND_CEX, pt.cex = 1, bty = "n",
         ncol = ceiling(length(node_order) / ROWS_PER_LEGEND_COL),
         title = "Taxa (colored by Phylum / Taxa2 / cyanobacteria Taxa)",
         title.cex = 0.62)

  # Reset to a single-panel layout so anything plotted after this
  # function returns (in the same R session) isn't stuck in a 2-panel
  # layout left over from this call.
  layout(1)
}

for (code in names(lake_results)) {
  r <- lake_results[[code]]

  hab_present <- intersect(HAB_TAXA, r$taxa)
  missing_hab <- setdiff(HAB_TAXA, r$taxa)
  if (length(missing_hab) > 0) {
    message("Lake ", code, ": HAB-list genera not present in this lake's filtered ",
            "network - ", paste(missing_hab, collapse = ", "))
  }

  if (length(hab_present) == 0) {
    message("Lake ", code, ": no HAB-list genera present - skipping")
    plot.new()
    title(main = paste0(lake_lookup[code], "\n(no HAB-list genera in filtered network)"))
    next
  }

  edges <- r$net$edgelist1

  partner_taxa <- character(0)
  for (tx in hab_present) {
    partner_taxa <- union(partner_taxa, get_top_n_partners(edges, tx, TOP_N_PARTNERS))
  }
  partner_taxa <- setdiff(partner_taxa, hab_present)

  neighbor_set <- sort(unique(c(hab_present, partner_taxa)))

  cat("Lake", code, "-", length(hab_present), "HAB-list genera present;",
      length(partner_taxa), "unique top-", TOP_N_PARTNERS, "partner(s) across them;",
      length(neighbor_set), "total nodes in this lake's HAB subnetwork\n")

  # Resolve color + legend label for every node in this lake's subnetwork,
  # once, before plotting - shared by both the svg() and on-screen render
  # calls below, and by the legend.
  resolved <- lapply(neighbor_set, function(tx) resolve_node_color(tx, r$domain[[tx]]))
  node_colors <- setNames(vapply(resolved, function(x) x$color, character(1)), neighbor_set)
  node_labels <- setNames(vapply(resolved, function(x) x$label, character(1)), neighbor_set)

  # Wider canvas (20 vs the previous 16) - numbers freed up space on the
  # ring itself, but the legend gained a few characters per row ("N. "
  # prefix) and may need up to 3 columns for Lake Rippowam's 78 nodes;
  # this keeps the legend text at a readable size (LEGEND_CEX = 0.52
  # above) without crowding the circle.
  # Widened again (24 vs the previous 20) now that the legend has its own
  # real panel width (LAYOUT_WIDTHS[2] = 0.42 of this total) instead of
  # sharing the circle's aspect-locked coordinate space - this is what
  # actually fixes the 3rd-column-runs-off-the-device problem; the extra
  # device width now translates directly into extra legend-panel width.
  svg(paste0("results/HAB_subnetwork_", code, ".svg"), width = 24, height = 10)
  plot_hab_subnetwork_circlize(code, neighbor_set, hab_present, partner_taxa, node_colors, node_labels)
  dev.off()

  plot_hab_subnetwork_circlize(code, neighbor_set, hab_present, partner_taxa, node_colors, node_labels)

  # Number column matches exactly what's drawn on the ring and listed in
  # the legend (both computed identically, from sort(neighbor_set), inside
  # plot_hab_subnetwork_circlize) - included here so the CSV can serve as
  # a caption-ready number-to-taxon key alongside the figure.
  node_number_ref <- setNames(seq_along(sort(neighbor_set)), sort(neighbor_set))
  neighbor_tables[[code]] <- data.frame(
    Lake = lake_lookup[code], Number = node_number_ref[neighbor_set], Taxon = neighbor_set,
    Domain = r$domain[neighbor_set], is_HAB = neighbor_set %in% HAB_TAXA,
    is_HAB_anchor = neighbor_set %in% hab_present,
    Legend_Label = node_labels[neighbor_set],
    Color = node_colors[neighbor_set],
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

neighbor_table_all <- do.call(rbind, neighbor_tables)
neighbor_table_all <- neighbor_table_all[order(neighbor_table_all$Lake, neighbor_table_all$Number), ]
write.csv(neighbor_table_all, "results/HAB_subnetwork_taxon_reference.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n=== HAB subnetwork taxon reference table (also written to CSV) ===\n")
print(neighbor_table_all)
```

# 8. Sorted diverging bar ("tornado") plot per HAB taxon

One panel per HAB-list genus present in a lake's filtered network: every
direct co-occurrence partner, sorted by `|association|`, bars extending
left (negative) or right (positive) of zero. Reuses `r$net$edgelist1` and
`r$domain` directly -- no statistic recomputed.

```{r hab-bars-function}
# =====================================================================
# Section 8 replacement, v2: "Sorted diverging bar ('tornado') plot per
# HAB taxon", now using:
#   - Partners: top TOP_N_PARTNERS (5) by |asso| per anchor taxon (same
#     get_top_n_partners() helper and same TOP_N_PARTNERS value already
#     defined in Section 7 v3 - NOT recomputed independently, so the two
#     sections can never disagree on what "top 5 by asso" means).
#   - Partner label color + text: resolve_node_color() from Section 7 v3
#     (Phylum for 16S, Taxa2 for 18S, bare Taxon for cyanobacteria) -
#     replaces the old 2-color 16S/18S domain scheme.
#
# REQUIRES Section 7 v3 (section7_v3_taxon_colors.R) to already be
# sourced/run - get_top_n_partners(), resolve_node_color(), safe_lookup(),
# and the three color lookup tables all come from there.
#
# Anchor taxa (which genera get a panel at all) are UNCHANGED from the
# previous version: top_hab_by_abundance[[code]], from the abundance-
# ranking chunk before this one - top 5 HAB_TAXA genera by mean relative
# abundance within Cyanobacteria, matching Figure 6.
# =====================================================================

if (!exists("resolve_node_color") || !exists("get_top_n_partners")) {
  stop("Section 8 v2 requires Section 7 v3 (section7_v3_taxon_colors.R) to be run first - ",
       "resolve_node_color() and get_top_n_partners() are not defined. Run that chunk, ",
       "then re-run this one.")
}

#' Plot the top-N co-occurrence partners of one HAB taxon by |association|,
#' colored and labeled using Section 7's resolve_node_color() (Phylum/
#' Taxa2/cyanobacteria-Taxa scheme), sorted by |asso|. Labels sit in a
#' single right-aligned column past the bars, so they never overlap a bar
#' regardless of association sign.
plot_hab_bars <- function(lake_code, taxon, top_n = TOP_N_PARTNERS) {
  r <- lake_results[[lake_code]]
  edges <- r$net$edgelist1

  top_partners <- get_top_n_partners(edges, taxon, top_n)

  if (length(top_partners) == 0) {
    message("Lake ", lake_code, ": '", taxon, "' has no edges in the filtered ",
            "network - skipping its bar panel")
    return(
      ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0,
                 label = paste0(taxon, "\n(no network edges)"), size = 4.2) +
        theme_void()
    )
  }

  touch <- edges$v1 == taxon | edges$v2 == taxon
  sub <- edges[touch, ]
  sub$partner <- ifelse(sub$v1 == taxon, sub$v2, sub$v1)
  sub <- sub[sub$partner %in% top_partners, ]
  sub$partner_domain <- r$domain[sub$partner]

  # Resolve each partner's color + display label (e.g. "Comamonas
  # (Proteobacteria)", or bare "Cyanobium" if the partner is itself
  # cyanobacteria) - same function Section 7's network figure uses, so a
  # given taxon's color is identical across every figure in the manuscript.
  resolved <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(sub)), function(i) {
    resolve_node_color(sub$partner[i], sub$partner_domain[i])
  })
  sub$partner_color <- vapply(resolved, function(x) x$color, character(1))
  sub$partner_label <- vapply(resolved, function(x) x$label, character(1))

  sub <- sub[order(abs(sub$asso)), ]
  # Factor levels stay the raw taxon name (preserves |asso| sort order);
  # the DISPLAYED text comes from label_lookup via scale_y_discrete()
  # below, ggplot's own axis-text mechanism - drawn in the plot margin,
  # outside the panel, so it can never collide with a bar regardless of
  # sign. Replaces the previous geom_text() column manually positioned
  # past the bars, which was only ever a workaround for not having used
  # a real axis to begin with.
  sub$partner <- factor(sub$partner, levels = sub$partner)
  label_lookup <- setNames(sub$partner_label, as.character(sub$partner))

  # CHANGED (per request): bar FILL is now the taxon color (Phylum/Taxa2/
  # cyanobacteria-Taxa, via scale_fill_identity()) - association direction
  # (positive/negative) is conveyed by bar position alone (left/right of
  # the zero line), no longer by color, since that role moved to the bars.
  # Axis text (right side, via scale_y_discrete position) is plain black
  # italic (genus-name convention) - the color-coding lives on the bar.
  ggplot(sub, aes(x = asso, y = partner)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = partner_color), width = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "gray40") +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = label_lookup, position = "right") +
    labs(x = "Association (symmetrized MB coefficient)", y = NULL,
         title = paste0(taxon, " - ", lake_lookup[lake_code])) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y  = element_text(face = "italic", size = 10),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      plot.title   = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9),
      axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10)
    )
}

for (code in names(lake_results)) {
  r <- lake_results[[code]]

  # Anchor taxa unchanged: top_hab_by_abundance[[code]] (top 5 HAB_TAXA
  # genera by mean relative abundance within Cyanobacteria, matching
  # Figure 6 - see the abundance-ranking chunk before Section 8).
  taxa_to_plot <- top_hab_by_abundance[[code]]

  if (length(taxa_to_plot) == 0) {
    message("Lake ", code, ": no abundance-ranked HAB genera available - skipping bar panels")
    next
  }

  panel_list <- lapply(taxa_to_plot, function(tx) plot_hab_bars(code, tx, top_n = TOP_N_PARTNERS))

  is_valid <- vapply(panel_list, function(x) inherits(x, "gg"), logical(1))
  if (!all(is_valid)) {
    stop("Lake ", code, ": plot_hab_bars() returned a non-ggplot object for ",
         "taxon/taxa: ", paste(taxa_to_plot[!is_valid], collapse = ", "),
         ". Fix plot_hab_bars() before proceeding - not skipping silently.")
  }

  # CHANGED (per request): single column, not a sqrt(n)-based grid - each
  # panel gets the figure's full width, leaving room for long taxonomic
  # names like "Burkholderiales_MWH-UniP1-aquatic-group_unclassified
  # (Proteobacteria)" that a multi-column layout would cramp or clip.
  n_taxa <- length(panel_list)
  n_row <- n_taxa
  n_col <- 1

  combined <- patchwork::wrap_plots(panel_list, nrow = n_row, ncol = n_col) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = paste0(lake_lookup[code], " - Top ", n_taxa, " HAB genera by abundance: ",
                      "top ", TOP_N_PARTNERS, " co-occurrence partners by |asso|"),
      theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"))
    )

  print(combined)

  # Wider fixed width (9in) now that there's only one column - the old
  # "4 * n_col" formula gave just 4in for n_col = 1, far too narrow for
  # the appended "(Phylum)"/"(Taxa2)" text. Height scales with panel count
  # as before (3.2in per row).
  ggsave(paste0("results/HAB_bars_top", TOP_N_ABUNDANT, "_", code, ".svg"), combined,
         width = 9, height = 3.2 * n_row, dpi = 300, limitsize = FALSE)
}
```

# =========================================================================
# 8a. Faceted heat map of HAB taxon x associated-taxon co-occurrence
#    Rows = HAB-list genera present in a lake's filtered network.
#    Columns = every direct co-occurrence partner of any HAB taxon in that
#    lake (may itself be a HAB genus). Cell value = symmetrized MB
#    association ("asso") from r$net$edgelist1 - no statistic recomputed,
#    same source data as the original Section 8 tornado plot.
#    One heat map per lake; panels share one color scale (see below) so
#    they are visually comparable, combined via gridExtra per pheatmap's
#    own documented pattern (silent=TRUE -> $gtable -> grid.arrange()).
# =========================================================================

```{r facet heat maps}
# =========================================================================
# 8a. Faceted heat map: partner universe = union of each anchor's own
#     top-N partners; cells filled with REAL asso value wherever an edge
#     exists in that universe; an asterisk marks cells that are a genus's
#     OWN top-N partner (via pheatmap's documented display_numbers matrix,
#     not a border overlay).
# =========================================================================

if (!exists("resolve_node_color") || !exists("get_top_n_partners")) stop("Run Section 7 v3 first.")
if (!exists("top_hab_by_abundance") || !exists("TOP_N_ABUNDANT")) stop("Run Section 7a first.")
required_pkgs <- c("pheatmap", "grid")
missing_pkgs  <- required_pkgs[!vapply(required_pkgs, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE, FUN.VALUE = logical(1))]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) stop("Missing package(s): ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "))
library(pheatmap); library(grid)

# ---- Step 1: partner universe = union of top-N; CELLS FILLED WITH REAL
# VALUES against that whole universe (not restricted to each genus's own
# top-N); top_mat flags which cells ARE that genus's own top-N ----
build_hab_heatmap_data <- function(lake_code, top_n = TOP_N_PARTNERS) {
  r <- lake_results[[lake_code]]
  edges <- r$net$edgelist1
  taxa_to_plot <- top_hab_by_abundance[[lake_code]]
  if (length(taxa_to_plot) == 0) {
    message("Lake ", lake_code, ": no abundance-ranked HAB genera - skipping heat map")
    return(NULL)
  }

  top_partners_per_taxon <- setNames(
    lapply(taxa_to_plot, function(tx) get_top_n_partners(edges, tx, top_n)), taxa_to_plot)
  partner_names <- sort(unique(unlist(top_partners_per_taxon)))
  if (length(partner_names) == 0) {
    message("Lake ", lake_code, ": no top-N partners found - skipping heat map")
    return(NULL)
  }

  mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(taxa_to_plot), ncol = length(partner_names),
                dimnames = list(taxa_to_plot, partner_names))
  top_mat <- matrix(FALSE, nrow = length(taxa_to_plot), ncol = length(partner_names),
                     dimnames = list(taxa_to_plot, partner_names))

  for (taxon in taxa_to_plot) {
    touch <- edges$v1 == taxon | edges$v2 == taxon
    sub <- edges[touch, ]
    if (nrow(sub) == 0) next
    sub$partner <- ifelse(sub$v1 == taxon, sub$v2, sub$v1)
    sub <- sub[sub$partner %in% partner_names, ]   # only restricts to the fixed column set
    if (nrow(sub) == 0) next
    mat[taxon, sub$partner] <- sub$asso                                   # REAL value, always
    top_mat[taxon, sub$partner] <- sub$partner %in% top_partners_per_taxon[[taxon]]  # flag only
  }

  resolve_one <- function(tx) resolve_node_color(tx, r$domain[[tx]])
  row_resolved <- lapply(taxa_to_plot, resolve_one)
  col_resolved <- lapply(partner_names, resolve_one)

  list(mat = mat, top_mat = top_mat,
       row_label = setNames(vapply(row_resolved, function(x) x$label, character(1)), taxa_to_plot),
       row_color = setNames(vapply(row_resolved, function(x) x$color, character(1)), taxa_to_plot),
       col_label = setNames(vapply(col_resolved, function(x) x$label, character(1)), partner_names),
       col_color = setNames(vapply(col_resolved, function(x) x$color, character(1)), partner_names))
}

# ---- Step 2 ----
lake_heat_data <- lapply(names(lake_results), build_hab_heatmap_data)
names(lake_heat_data) <- names(lake_results)
lake_heat_data <- lake_heat_data[!vapply(lake_heat_data, is.null, logical(1))]
if (length(lake_heat_data) == 0) stop("No lake had usable HAB genus/partner data.")

# ---- Step 3 ----
max_abs_asso <- max(abs(unlist(lapply(lake_heat_data, function(d) d$mat[!is.na(d$mat)]))))
breaks_seq   <- seq(-max_abs_asso, max_abs_asso, length.out = 101)
heat_colors  <- colorRampPalette(c(COL_EDGE_NEG, "white", COL_EDGE_POS))(100)

# ---- Step 4 ----
lake_order <- names(lake_heat_data)
col_ids <- character(0); col_labels <- character(0); col_lake <- character(0); col_color <- character(0)
for (code in lake_order) {
  d <- lake_heat_data[[code]]
  genera <- rownames(d$mat)
  col_ids    <- c(col_ids, paste0(genera, "__", code))
  col_labels <- c(col_labels, d$row_label[genera])
  col_lake   <- c(col_lake, rep(lake_lookup[code], length(genera)))
  col_color  <- c(col_color, d$row_color[genera])
}

# ---- Step 5 ----
partner_label_lookup <- character(0); partner_color_lookup <- character(0)
for (code in lake_order) {
  d <- lake_heat_data[[code]]
  new_partners <- setdiff(colnames(d$mat), names(partner_label_lookup))
  if (length(new_partners) > 0) {
    partner_label_lookup[new_partners] <- d$col_label[new_partners]
    partner_color_lookup[new_partners] <- d$col_color[new_partners]
  }
}

# ---- Step 6 ----
all_partners_raw <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(lake_heat_data, function(d) colnames(d$mat)))))
extract_group <- function(label) {
  has_paren <- grepl("\\(.*\\)$", label)
  ifelse(has_paren, sub("^.*\\((.*)\\)$", "\\1", label), "Cyanobacteria (genus-level)")
}
partner_group_lookup <- setNames(extract_group(partner_label_lookup[all_partners_raw]), all_partners_raw)
all_partners <- all_partners_raw[order(partner_group_lookup[all_partners_raw], all_partners_raw)]

# ---- Step 7: combined_mat AND combined_top_mask ----
combined_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(all_partners), ncol = length(col_ids),
                        dimnames = list(all_partners, col_ids))
combined_top_mask <- matrix(FALSE, nrow = length(all_partners), ncol = length(col_ids),
                             dimnames = list(all_partners, col_ids))
for (code in lake_order) {
  d <- lake_heat_data[[code]]
  genera <- rownames(d$mat)
  ids    <- paste0(genera, "__", code)
  tmat     <- t(d$mat)
  tmat_top <- t(d$top_mat)
  combined_mat[rownames(tmat), ids]          <- tmat
  combined_top_mask[rownames(tmat_top), ids] <- tmat_top
}

# ---- Step 8 ----
row_group_ordered <- partner_group_lookup[all_partners]
group_counts <- table(factor(row_group_ordered, levels = unique(row_group_ordered)))
gap_row_positions <- cumsum(group_counts); gap_row_positions <- gap_row_positions[-length(gap_row_positions)]
lake_col_counts <- table(factor(col_lake, levels = lake_lookup[lake_order]))
gap_col_positions <- cumsum(lake_col_counts); gap_col_positions <- gap_col_positions[-length(gap_col_positions)]

# ---- Step 9 ----
col_group_lookup <- setNames(extract_group(col_labels), col_ids)
row_ann <- data.frame(Taxon = partner_group_lookup[rownames(combined_mat)], row.names = rownames(combined_mat))
col_ann <- data.frame(Lake = col_lake, Taxon = col_group_lookup[col_ids], row.names = col_ids)

group_to_color <- character(0)
all_labels_and_colors <- c(setNames(col_color, col_labels), setNames(partner_color_lookup, partner_label_lookup))
all_groups_by_label <- extract_group(names(all_labels_and_colors))
for (i in seq_along(all_labels_and_colors)) {
  g <- all_groups_by_label[i]
  if (!(g %in% names(group_to_color))) group_to_color[g] <- all_labels_and_colors[i]
}
LAKE_COLORS <- setNames(c("#3498DB", "#E69F00", "#999999")[seq_along(lake_order)], lake_lookup[lake_order])
ann_colors <- list(Taxon = group_to_color, Lake = LAKE_COLORS)

# ---- Step 10: build the asterisk matrix (pheatmap's documented
# display_numbers pattern), aligned to combined_mat's FINAL row/col order ----
top_mask_ordered <- combined_top_mask[rownames(combined_mat), colnames(combined_mat)]
star_mat <- matrix(ifelse(top_mask_ordered, "*", ""),
                    nrow = nrow(combined_mat), ncol = ncol(combined_mat))

CELLWIDTH_PT <- 10; CELLHEIGHT_PT <- 10

hp <- pheatmap(combined_mat,
                color = heat_colors, breaks = breaks_seq, na_col = "grey89",
                cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
                gaps_row = as.integer(gap_row_positions), gaps_col = as.integer(gap_col_positions),
                cellwidth = CELLWIDTH_PT, cellheight = CELLHEIGHT_PT,
                labels_row = partner_label_lookup[rownames(combined_mat)], labels_col = col_labels,
                annotation_row = row_ann, annotation_col = col_ann,
                annotation_legend = TRUE, annotation_colors = ann_colors,
                display_numbers = star_mat,           # asterisk = this genus's own top-N partner
                number_color = "black", fontsize_number = 10,
                fontsize_row = 10, fontsize_col = 10, angle_col = 45,
                main = paste0("Top HAB genera by abundance x top ", TOP_N_PARTNERS,
                               " co-occurrence partners by |asso| (symmetrized MB coefficient).\n",
                               "* = this genus's own top ", TOP_N_PARTNERS, " partner by |asso|"),
                silent = TRUE)

required_width_in  <- grid::convertWidth(sum(hp$gtable$widths),  "in", valueOnly = TRUE)
required_height_in <- grid::convertHeight(sum(hp$gtable$heights), "in", valueOnly = TRUE)
cat("Measured gtable size:", round(required_width_in, 2), "in x", round(required_height_in, 2), "in\n")

grid.newpage()
grid.draw(hp$gtable)

svg(paste0("results/HAB_heatmap_top", TOP_N_ABUNDANT, "_all_lakes.svg"),
    width = required_width_in, height = required_height_in)
grid.draw(hp$gtable)
dev.off()
```

# 9. Cross-lake network comparison (`NetCoMi::netCompare`)

`netCompare()` requires the same taxon set in both networks being
compared, so this is restricted to taxa passing the prevalence filter in
**both** lakes. Permutation p-values are unavailable when comparing
precomputed association matrices rather than raw counts (documented
SpiecEasi/NetCoMi limitation), so `permTest = FALSE` -- this yields
descriptive, not p-value-based, comparison of network structure (see
Results outline Section 1.2/5.3).

```{r netcompare}
lake_codes <- names(lake_results)
lake_pairs <- combn(lake_codes, 2, simplify = FALSE)
netcompare_results <- list()

for (pair in lake_pairs) {
  a <- pair[1]; b <- pair[2]
  shared_taxa <- intersect(lake_results[[a]]$taxa, lake_results[[b]]$taxa)

  if (length(shared_taxa) < 3) {
    message("Skipping ", a, " vs ", b, ": fewer than 3 shared taxa after filtering.")
    next
  }

  assoA <- lake_results[[a]]$assoMat[shared_taxa, shared_taxa]
  assoB <- lake_results[[b]]$assoMat[shared_taxa, shared_taxa]

  netC   <- NetCoMi::netConstruct(data = assoA, data2 = assoB,
                                   dataType = "condDependence", sparsMethod = "none")
  propsC <- NetCoMi::netAnalyze(netC, hubPar = "eigenvector", clustMethod = "cluster_fast_greedy")
  compC  <- NetCoMi::netCompare(propsC, permTest = FALSE)

  netcompare_results[[paste(a, b, sep = "_vs_")]] <- compC
  cat("\n=== Network comparison:", a, "vs", b, "(", length(shared_taxa), "shared taxa) ===\n")
  print(summary(compC, groupNames = c(a, b)))

  # Export this comparison to a text file. capture.output() records exactly
  # what summary() already prints to console (global network properties,
  # centrality comparisons, Jaccard index of hub overlap, Rand index, and
  # Graphlet Correlation Distance) - this is the reliable export path since
  # NetCoMi's own help pages do not fully document every internal field name
  # of the returned microNetComp object, so extracting a specific field
  # directly (e.g. into a CSV) risks guessing at names that may not exist or
  # may differ by NetCoMi version.
  comp_txt <- capture.output({
    cat("Network comparison:", a, "vs", b, "\n")
    cat("Shared taxa (nodes) used in comparison:", length(shared_taxa), "\n\n")
    print(summary(compC, groupNames = c(a, b)))
  })
  writeLines(comp_txt, paste0("results/netcompare_", a, "_vs_", b, ".txt"))
}

# Combined file with all pairwise comparisons together, for convenience
all_comp_txt <- unlist(lapply(names(netcompare_results), function(nm) {
  parts <- strsplit(nm, "_vs_")[[1]]
  c("", "", paste("=== Network comparison:", parts[1], "vs", parts[2], "==="),
    capture.output(print(summary(netcompare_results[[nm]], groupNames = parts))))
}))
writeLines(all_comp_txt, "results/netcompare_all_comparisons.txt")
cat("\nSection 9 exported to results/netcompare_<lake>_vs_<lake>.txt (one file per pair)",
    "\nand results/netcompare_all_comparisons.txt (all pairs combined).\n")

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structured (non-text) exports and a combined GCD + Jaccard figure.
#
# netcompare_results is populated in the loop above (one microNetComp
# object per lake pair). Fields extracted below are limited to those
# NetCoMi's own documentation confirms:
# https://netcomi.de/reference/netcompare ("Value" section).
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ----- Global properties (documented field: diffGlobal - a named vector of
# differences for the 10 global network properties) -----
global_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(netcompare_results), function(nm) {
  cc <- netcompare_results[[nm]]
  data.frame(
    comparison = nm,
    property   = names(cc$diffGlobal),
    difference = as.numeric(cc$diffGlobal),
    row.names  = NULL
  )
}))
write.csv(global_summary, "results/netcompare_global_properties.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# ----- Graphlet Correlation Distance (GCD) -----
# calcGCD() - the function netCompare() calls internally to populate $gcd
# and $gcdLCC - documents its return value as a list with elements gcd,
# ocount1, ocount2, gcm1, gcm2 (https://rdrr.io/github/stefpeschel/NetCoMi/
# src/R/calcGCD.R). The scalar distance is therefore cc$gcd$gcd, NOT
# cc$gcd[1] (single-bracket indexing on a list returns a length-1 LIST,
# not a bare number, which would silently break the data.frame/plot below).
gcd_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(netcompare_results), function(nm) {
  cc <- netcompare_results[[nm]]
  data.frame(comparison   = nm,
             GCD_wholeNet = cc$gcd$gcd,
             GCD_LCC      = cc$gcdLCC$gcd)
}))
write.csv(gcd_summary, "results/netcompare_gcd.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# ----- Jaccard index (overlap of most-central nodes per centrality type) -----
# NetCoMi's documentation confirms jaccDeg/jaccBetw/jaccClose/jaccEigen/
# jaccHub hold "Values of Jaccard's index for the centrality measures," but
# does NOT specify the internal element names within each (the printed
# summary shows a Jacc value plus two p-values per row, so each is some
# short vector/list - exact names unconfirmed in the public docs). Rather
# than guess - the same caution already applied to $hubs in Section 15 -
# the Jacc values are parsed from the summary() print text captured just
# above, whose row format is fixed by NetCoMi's own summary.microNetComp()
# method and matches the official documentation example exactly.
jacc_labels <- c("degree", "betweenness centr.", "closeness centr.",
                  "eigenvec. centr.", "hub taxa")

parse_jaccard_block <- function(summary_lines) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(jacc_labels, function(lab) {
    esc <- gsub("([.])", "\\\\.", lab)
    ln  <- grep(paste0("^", esc), trimws(summary_lines), value = TRUE)

    if (length(ln) == 0) {
      return(data.frame(centrality = lab, Jacc = NA_real_,
                         P_le_Jacc = NA_real_, sig_le = ""))
    }

    # Tokens remaining after stripping the row label, in the fixed column
    # order NetCoMi's summary.microNetComp() prints: Jacc, P(<=Jacc),
    # [optional sig. code], P(>=Jacc), [optional sig. code]
    tokens <- strsplit(trimws(sub(lab, "", ln[1], fixed = TRUE)), "\\s+")[[1]]

    jacc_val <- as.numeric(tokens[1])
    p_le     <- as.numeric(tokens[2])

    # A significance-code token is one of ***, **, *, . per NetCoMi's own
    # printed footer ("Significance codes: ***: 0.001, **: 0.01, *: 0.05,
    # .: 0.1"). If tokens[3] matches this pattern, it belongs to P(<=Jacc),
    # not P(>=Jacc) - confirmed against the format in netcompare_all_
    # comparisons.txt (e.g. "0.137    0.000001 ***  1.000000").
    is_sig_code <- grepl("^(\\*{1,3}|\\.)$", tokens[3])
    sig_le <- if (is_sig_code) tokens[3] else ""

    data.frame(centrality = lab, Jacc = jacc_val,
               P_le_Jacc = p_le, sig_le = sig_le)
  }))
}

jacc_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(netcompare_results), function(nm) {
  parts <- strsplit(nm, "_vs_")[[1]]
  lines <- capture.output(print(summary(netcompare_results[[nm]], groupNames = parts)))
  df <- parse_jaccard_block(lines)
  df$comparison <- nm
  df
}))
write.csv(jacc_summary, "results/netcompare_jaccard.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# ----- Combined 2-panel figure: GCD (left) + Jaccard index (right) -----

PAIR_COLORS <- setNames(c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73"), names(netcompare_results))

p_gcd <- ggplot(gcd_summary, aes(x = comparison, y = GCD_wholeNet, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +   # FIXED: explicit width, matched to panel B's bar width below
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAIR_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Lake pair", y = "GCD",
       title = "Structural dissimilarity (GCD)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

p_jacc <- ggplot(jacc_summary, aes(x = centrality, y = Jacc, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = position_dodge(width = 0.7, preserve = "single")) +
  # Significance stars for P(<=Jacc), positioned above each dodged bar -
  # group = comparison keeps each star aligned with its own bar rather
  # than all three collapsing to one x position
  geom_text(aes(label = sig_le, group = comparison),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
            vjust = -0.3, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAIR_COLORS, name = "Lake pair") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(10)) +
  # Extra headroom above the tallest bar so stars aren't clipped
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Jaccard index",
       title = "Overlap of most-central nodes",
       caption = "Stars = significance of P(\u2264Jacc): *** p<0.001, ** p<0.01") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 0))

p_netcompare <- (p_gcd + p_jacc) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1.6)) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
print(p_netcompare)
ggsave("results/netcompare_gcd_jaccard_plot.png", p_netcompare,
       width = 10, height = 4, dpi = 300)
ggsave("results/netcompare_gcd_jaccard_plot.svg", p_netcompare,
       width = 10, height = 4, dpi = 600)

```

# 10. Environmental (abiotic) associations

**(a)** Community level: Mantel test (Bray-Curtis vs. scaled Euclidean
environmental distance). **(b)** Cyanobacteria-focused: Spearman
correlation per Taxa entry per environmental variable, BH-FDR corrected
across the full pre-specified family of tests (all lakes, all
Cyanobacteria taxa, all 10 environmental variables).

Relative abundance is computed by normalizing the 16S and 18S count
matrices to **their own totals separately**, then combining -- not by
dividing by a single combined 16S+18S total. 16S and 18S sequencing depth
per sample are independent, arbitrary quantities (driven by primer
efficiency / sequencing effort allocation), so a shared denominator would
let each sample's arbitrary 16S:18S read-depth ratio contaminate every
taxon's apparent relative abundance. This differs from Sections 5-9 above,
where raw counts are passed directly to SpiecEasi, which performs its own
internal normalization/CLR transform -- pre-normalizing before that step
would double-transform the data.

```{r spearman-helper}
spearman_naomit <- function(x, y) {
  ok <- complete.cases(x, y)
  if (sum(ok) < 4) return(c(rho = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, n = sum(ok)))
  ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(x[ok], y[ok], method = "spearman"))
  c(rho = unname(ct$estimate), p = ct$p.value, n = sum(ok))
}
```

```{r env-associations}
mantel_results <- list()
cyano_env_rows <- list()
lake_env_store <- list()# per-lake relative abundance + raw env data, for Section 11/12
mantel_diagnostics <- list()

for (code in names(lake_results)) {
  r <- lake_results[[code]]
  samp_ids <- r$samples

  env_lake <- meta[match(samp_ids, meta$SampleShort), env_vars_all]
  rownames(env_lake) <- samp_ids

  # Unfiltered copy of this lake's environmental data (all 10 variables,
  # own NAs) BEFORE the Mantel-specific >20%-missing column drop below.
  # FIXED (Rmd review, bug #1): this object is now also used by the
  # taxon-level loop further down, not just by Sections 11/12 - see note
  # at that loop.
  env_lake_raw <- env_lake

  # Drop environmental variables from THIS LAKE'S MANTEL TEST ONLY if
  # missing in >20% of this lake's samples (covers variables missing
  # entirely, e.g. Btemp/BDO for an unstratified lake, and variables with
  # heavy partial missingness, e.g. PO4/N:P). Flagged explicitly, never
  # dropped silently.
  missing_frac <- sapply(env_lake, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))
  drop_cols <- names(missing_frac)[missing_frac > 0.20]
  if (length(drop_cols) > 0) {
    message("Lake ", code, ": environmental variable(s) excluded from the MANTEL TEST ONLY ",
             "(missing in >20% of samples): ",
             paste0(drop_cols, " (", round(missing_frac[drop_cols] * 100), "% missing)",
                    collapse = ", "))
    env_lake <- env_lake[, setdiff(names(env_lake), drop_cols), drop = FALSE]
  }

  # --- (a) Community-level Mantel test -----------------------------------
  rel_16 <- apply(r$m16[, paste0("16S-", samp_ids)], 2, function(x) x / sum(x))
  rel_18 <- apply(r$m18[, paste0("18S-", samp_ids)], 2, function(x) x / sum(x))
  rel_abund <- rbind(rel_16, rel_18)
  colnames(rel_abund) <- samp_ids
  bio_dist_full <- vegan::vegdist(t(rel_abund), method = "bray")

  lake_env_store[[code]] <- list(rel_abund = rel_abund, env_lake_raw = env_lake_raw)

  complete_idx <- complete.cases(env_lake)
  n_dropped <- sum(!complete_idx)
  if (n_dropped > 0) {
    message("Lake ", code, ": Mantel test uses ", sum(complete_idx), " of ",
            nrow(env_lake), " samples (", n_dropped,
            " excluded due to missing environmental data for THIS TEST ONLY)")
  }

  env_dist    <- dist(scale(env_lake[complete_idx, , drop = FALSE]))
  bio_dist_sub <- as.dist(as.matrix(bio_dist_full)[complete_idx, complete_idx])

  mantel_results[[code]] <- vegan::mantel(bio_dist_sub, env_dist, method = "spearman", permutations = 999)
  # Store per-lake Mantel-test diagnostics (sample size and environmental-
  # variable set actually used) alongside the mantel object itself, since
  # these aren't part of the mantel-class object's own documented fields
  # but are needed for a complete supplemental-table record.
  mantel_diagnostics[[code]] <- list(
  n_used        = sum(complete_idx),
  n_total       = nrow(env_lake_raw),
  env_vars_used = names(env_lake),          # after the >20%-missing drop, this lake only
  env_vars_dropped = drop_cols               # variables excluded from THIS lake's Mantel test
    )
  cat("\nLake", code, "- Mantel test (community structure vs. environment):\n")
  print(mantel_results[[code]])

  # --- (b) Cyanobacteria taxon x environmental variable correlations -----
  cyano_in_lake <- intersect(cyano_taxa, rownames(r$m16))
  if (length(cyano_in_lake) == 0) {
    message("Lake ", code, ": no Cyanobacteria taxa passed the prevalence filter - ",
            "skipping taxon-level correlation for this lake")
    next
  }

  cyano_rel <- rel_abund[cyano_in_lake, , drop = FALSE]

  # FIXED (Rmd review, bug #1): loop over env_lake_raw (the FULL
  # pre-specified 10-variable set for this lake), NOT env_lake (which had
  # columns dropped above for the Mantel test specifically). The original
  # script's own comment said taxon-level tests were "unaffected" by the
  # Mantel-test column drop; the code did not match that comment. Using
  # env_lake_raw here makes the code match the comment and keeps the tested
  # family of taxon x variable pairs the full pre-specified set (Results
  # outline Section 4.2), with missingness handled per-pair by
  # spearman_naomit()'s complete.cases(), not by dropping the variable
  # for every taxon in the lake.
  for (tx in cyano_in_lake) {
    for (v in names(env_lake_raw)) {
      res <- spearman_naomit(cyano_rel[tx, ], env_lake_raw[[v]])
      cyano_env_rows[[length(cyano_env_rows) + 1]] <-
        data.frame(lake = lake_lookup[code], taxon = tx, env_var = v,
                   rho = res["rho"], p_value = res["p"], n = res["n"])
    }
  }
}

# Build one row per lake from vegan::mantel() output. Field names (statistic,
# signif, permutations, method) are exactly as documented for objects of
# class "mantel" - https://vegandevs.github.io/vegan/reference/mantel.html
mantel_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(mantel_results), function(code) {
  m    <- mantel_results[[code]]
  diag <- mantel_diagnostics[[code]]

  data.frame(
    Lake                      = lake_lookup[code],
    Correlation_method        = m$method,
    Mantel_r                  = m$statistic,
    p_value                   = m$signif,
    Permutations              = m$permutations,
    N_samples_used            = diag$n_used,
    N_samples_total           = diag$n_total,
    N_env_vars_used           = length(diag$env_vars_used),
    Env_vars_used             = paste(diag$env_vars_used, collapse = "; "),
    Env_vars_excluded_missing = if (length(diag$env_vars_dropped) > 0)
                                   paste(diag$env_vars_dropped, collapse = "; ") else "None",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    row.names = NULL
  )
}))

write.csv(mantel_table, "results/mantel_test_summary_table.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n=== Mantel test summary table (also written to mantel_test_summary_table.csv) ===\n")
print(mantel_table)

cyano_env_table <- do.call(rbind, cyano_env_rows)
cyano_env_table$p_adj_BH <- p.adjust(cyano_env_table$p_value, method = "BH")
cyano_env_table$is_HAB <- cyano_env_table$taxon %in% HAB_TAXA
cyano_env_table <- cyano_env_table[order(cyano_env_table$p_adj_BH), ]

write.csv(cyano_env_table, "results/cyanobacteria_environment_correlations.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nCyanobacteria-environment correlations (BH-FDR corrected), top results:\n")
print(head(cyano_env_table, 15))
cat("\n=== HAB-list genus x environment correlations only (BH-FDR corrected) ===\n")
print(cyano_env_table[cyano_env_table$is_HAB, ])
```

# 11. HAB-focused environment correlation heatmap (per lake)

Base R only (no extra plotting dependency): a taxon x environmental-variable
grid of Spearman rho, with the BH-adjusted p-value overlaid so significance
and effect size are both visible in one figure.

```{r env-heatmap}
# =========================================================================
# 11 (pheatmap version). HAB genus x environmental-variable Spearman rho,
# split by lake via gaps_col, uniform cell size via pheatmap's cellwidth/
# cellheight - replaces the ggplot2 facet_wrap version. Same source data
# (cyano_env_table, Section 10), same BH-adjusted significance tiers, same
# "drop all-NA lake x env_var combos" filtering as the last revision.
# =========================================================================

required_pkgs <- c("pheatmap", "grid")
missing_pkgs  <- required_pkgs[!vapply(required_pkgs, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE, FUN.VALUE = logical(1))]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) stop("Missing package(s): ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "))
library(pheatmap); library(grid)

hab_env_plot_data <- cyano_env_table[cyano_env_table$is_HAB, ]
if (nrow(hab_env_plot_data) == 0) stop("No HAB-list genus x environment data to plot.")

hab_env_plot_data$lake <- factor(hab_env_plot_data$lake, levels = lake_lookup[names(lake_lookup)])

# ---- Drop (lake, env_var) combos with no non-NA rho among HAB genera in
# that lake - same filtering step as the ggplot version ----
combo_has_value <- with(hab_env_plot_data,
                         tapply(rho, list(lake, env_var), function(x) any(!is.na(x))))
combo_has_value[is.na(combo_has_value)] <- FALSE

keep_idx <- mapply(function(lk, ev) isTRUE(combo_has_value[as.character(lk), ev]),
                    hab_env_plot_data$lake, hab_env_plot_data$env_var)
n_dropped <- sum(!keep_idx)
if (n_dropped > 0) {
  dropped_summary <- unique(hab_env_plot_data[!keep_idx, c("lake", "env_var")])
  message("Section 11: dropping ", nrow(dropped_summary), " lake x env_var combination(s) ",
          "with no non-NA rho among HAB genera:")
  print(dropped_summary)
}
hab_env_plot_data <- hab_env_plot_data[keep_idx, ]

sig_stars <- function(p) {
  ifelse(is.na(p), "",
         ifelse(p < 0.001, "***",
                ifelse(p < 0.01, "**",
                       ifelse(p < 0.05, "*", ""))))
}

# ---- Build column set: env_var per lake, unique matrix IDs, only the
# combos that survived filtering above ----
lake_order <- levels(hab_env_plot_data$lake)
col_ids <- character(0); col_env_var <- character(0); col_lake <- character(0)

for (lk in lake_order) {
  evs <- sort(unique(hab_env_plot_data$env_var[hab_env_plot_data$lake == lk]))
  if (length(evs) == 0) next
  col_ids     <- c(col_ids, paste0(evs, "__", lk))
  col_env_var <- c(col_env_var, evs)
  col_lake    <- c(col_lake, rep(lk, length(evs)))
}

# ---- Row set: union of HAB genera across all lakes (alphabetical) ----
all_taxa <- sort(unique(hab_env_plot_data$taxon))

# ---- Build matrices: rho values, and rho+stars text for display_numbers ----
rho_mat  <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(all_taxa), ncol = length(col_ids),
                    dimnames = list(all_taxa, col_ids))
star_mat <- matrix("", nrow = length(all_taxa), ncol = length(col_ids),
                    dimnames = list(all_taxa, col_ids))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(hab_env_plot_data))) {
  row <- hab_env_plot_data[i, ]
  cid <- paste0(row$env_var, "__", as.character(row$lake))
  if (!(cid %in% col_ids)) next   # filtered-out combo
  if (is.na(row$rho)) next        # this specific taxon has no value even though the column survived
  rho_mat[row$taxon, cid]  <- row$rho
  star_mat[row$taxon, cid] <- sprintf("%.2f%s", row$rho, sig_stars(row$p_adj_BH))
}

# ---- gaps_col by lake ----
lake_col_counts <- table(factor(col_lake, levels = lake_order))
gap_col_positions <- cumsum(lake_col_counts)
gap_col_positions <- gap_col_positions[-length(gap_col_positions)]

col_ann <- data.frame(Lake = col_lake, row.names = col_ids)
LAKE_COLORS <- setNames(c("#3498DB", "#E69F00", "#999999")[seq_along(lake_order)], lake_order)
ann_colors <- list(Lake = LAKE_COLORS)

# ---- Fixed color scale at [-1, 1] (rho's natural bounds), matching the
# ggplot version's scale_fill_gradient2(limits = c(-1, 1)) rather than a
# data-driven max - keeps cross-panel comparison meaningful ----
breaks_seq  <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = 101)
heat_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#0072B2", "white", "#D55E00"))(100)

CELLWIDTH_PT <- 18; CELLHEIGHT_PT <- 18

hp <- pheatmap(rho_mat,
                color = heat_colors, breaks = breaks_seq, na_col = "grey85",
                cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
                gaps_col = as.integer(gap_col_positions),
                cellwidth = CELLWIDTH_PT, cellheight = CELLHEIGHT_PT,
                labels_col = col_env_var,
                annotation_col = col_ann, annotation_colors = ann_colors,
                display_numbers = star_mat, number_color = "black",
                fontsize_number = 7,
                fontsize_row = 10, fontsize_col = 10, angle_col = 45,
                main = "HAB-list genus x environmental variable (Spearman rho, BH-adjusted)",
                silent = TRUE)

required_width_in  <- grid::convertWidth(sum(hp$gtable$widths),  "in", valueOnly = TRUE)
required_height_in <- grid::convertHeight(sum(hp$gtable$heights), "in", valueOnly = TRUE)
cat("Measured gtable size:", round(required_width_in, 2), "in x", round(required_height_in, 2), "in\n")

grid.newpage()
grid.draw(hp$gtable)

svg("results/HAB_environment_correlation_heatmap_pheatmap.svg",
    width = required_width_in, height = required_height_in)
grid.draw(hp$gtable)
dev.off()

cat("\nCells show Spearman rho (text) with BH-adjusted significance tiers:\n")
cat("'*' p_adj_BH < 0.05, '**' p_adj_BH < 0.01, '***' p_adj_BH < 0.001.\n")
cat("Grey cells = no correlation available for that taxon in that lake ",
    "(taxon absent, or excluded by prevalence filtering) - not zero or non-significant.\n")
```

# 12. Taxon-specific relative-abundance vs. environmental-variable plots

For inspecting one flagged correlation directly rather than relying on the
heatmap alone. Works for any taxon in a lake's stored relative-abundance
matrix. Rho/p values are pulled directly from `cyano_env_table` (already
computed in Section 10) rather than recomputed, so the plot always matches
what was tested/reported.

```{r taxon-vs-env-function}
plot_taxon_vs_env <- function(lake_code, taxon, env_var, corr_table = cyano_env_table) {
  dat <- lake_env_store[[lake_code]]
  if (is.null(dat)) {
    stop("No stored data for lake code '", lake_code, "'. Valid codes: ",
         paste(names(lake_env_store), collapse = ", "))
  }
  if (!(taxon %in% rownames(dat$rel_abund))) {
    stop("Taxon '", taxon, "' not found in lake '", lake_code, "'s relative-abundance ",
         "matrix - either absent from raw data, or removed by the ", min_prevalence * 100,
         "% prevalence filter (check that lake's console output above).")
  }
  if (!(env_var %in% names(dat$env_lake_raw))) {
    stop("Environmental variable '", env_var, "' not recognized. Available: ",
         paste(names(dat$env_lake_raw), collapse = ", "))
  }

  x <- dat$env_lake_raw[[env_var]]
  y <- dat$rel_abund[taxon, ] * 100
  ok <- complete.cases(x, y)
  n_dropped <- sum(!ok)
  if (n_dropped > 0) {
    message(lake_code, " - ", taxon, " vs ", env_var, ": ", n_dropped,
            " sample(s) excluded from this plot (missing ", env_var, " data)")
  }

  plot_df <- data.frame(x = x[ok], y = y[ok])

  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_point(color = COL_CYANO, size = 2.6) +
    labs(x = env_var, y = paste0(taxon, " relative abundance (%)"),
         title = paste0(lake_lookup[lake_code], ": ", taxon, " vs. ", env_var)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 9))

  if (sum(ok) >= 3) {
    p <- p + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
                          color = COL_16S_OTHER, linewidth = 0.8)
  }

  stat_row <- corr_table[corr_table$lake == lake_lookup[lake_code] &
                            corr_table$taxon == taxon & corr_table$env_var == env_var, ]
  if (nrow(stat_row) == 1) {
    stat_label <- sprintf("Spearman rho = %.2f\nBH-adj p = %.3f (n=%d)",
                           stat_row$rho, stat_row$p_adj_BH, stat_row$n)
    p <- p + annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = stat_label,
                       hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.2, size = 2.8)
  } else {
    message("Note: no matching row for ", taxon, " x ", env_var, " in ", lake_code,
            " - statistic not annotated on plot.")
  }

  # ADDED: OLS annotation, merged directly into this function (previously
  # pasted as a disconnected top-level fragment in a separate chunk, where
  # lake_code/taxon/env_var didn't exist as objects - that's what produced
  # "object 'lake_code' not found"). fit_taxon_env_lm() must be defined
  # before this function is called - see the chunk below.
  lm_result <- fit_taxon_env_lm(lake_code, taxon, env_var)
  if (!is.null(lm_result)) {
    lm_label <- sprintf("OLS: R\u00b2 = %.2f, p = %.3f (n=%d)",
                         lm_result$r_squared, lm_result$p_value, lm_result$n)
    p <- p + annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = lm_label,
                       hjust = -0.05, vjust = 3.0, size = 2.8, color = "gray30")
  }

  p
}
```

```{r taxon-vs-env-render}
# Example plots - swap taxon/env_var/lake arguments for any combination
# flagged in cyanobacteria_environment_correlations.csv
p_taxon_env <- plot_taxon_vs_env("LR", "Planktothrix", "MC")
ggsave("results/LR_planktovsMC.svg", p_taxon_env,
       width = 4, height = 4, device = "svg")
```

```{r lm model}
#' Fit an OLS linear model for one taxon x environmental-variable pair,
#' using the SAME complete-case data as plot_taxon_vs_env() (same x, y,
#' same missing-data handling) - not a separate/different dataset.
#' Reported as a SEPARATE, uncorrected single test, since it was not part
#' of the pre-specified family that Section 10's p.adjust(method = "BH")
#' was applied across.
fit_taxon_env_lm <- function(lake_code, taxon, env_var) {
  dat <- lake_env_store[[lake_code]]
  if (is.null(dat)) stop("No stored data for lake code '", lake_code, "'.")
  if (!(taxon %in% rownames(dat$rel_abund))) {
    stop("Taxon '", taxon, "' not found in lake '", lake_code, "'s relative-abundance matrix.")
  }
  if (!(env_var %in% names(dat$env_lake_raw))) {
    stop("Environmental variable '", env_var, "' not recognized.")
  }

  x <- dat$env_lake_raw[[env_var]]
  y <- dat$rel_abund[taxon, ] * 100
  ok <- complete.cases(x, y)
  n_dropped <- sum(!ok)
  if (n_dropped > 0) {
    message(lake_code, " - ", taxon, " vs ", env_var, " (lm): ", n_dropped,
            " sample(s) excluded (missing ", env_var, " data)")
  }
  if (sum(ok) < 4) {
    warning(lake_code, " - ", taxon, " vs ", env_var, ": fewer than 4 complete cases (n=",
             sum(ok), ") - OLS estimates would be unreliable at this sample size. Not fitting.")
    return(NULL)
  }

  fit <- lm(y[ok] ~ x[ok])
  s <- summary(fit)

  list(
    n = sum(ok),
    slope = unname(coef(fit)[2]),
    intercept = unname(coef(fit)[1]),
    r_squared = s$r.squared,
    adj_r_squared = s$adj.r.squared,
    f_statistic = unname(s$fstatistic["value"]),
    df1 = unname(s$fstatistic["numdf"]),
    df2 = unname(s$fstatistic["dendf"]),
    p_value = pf(s$fstatistic["value"], s$fstatistic["numdf"], s$fstatistic["dendf"],
                 lower.tail = FALSE),
    model = fit
  )
}

# Render (unchanged call, now also computes/prints the lm result)
p_taxon_env <- plot_taxon_vs_env("LR", "Planktothrix", "MC")
lm_check <- fit_taxon_env_lm("LR", "Planktothrix", "MC")
cat("OLS fit, Lake Rippowam Planktothrix vs MC:\n")
cat("  slope =", round(lm_check$slope, 3), " R-squared =", round(lm_check$r_squared, 3),
    " p =", signif(lm_check$p_value, 3), " (n=", lm_check$n, ", NOT BH-adjusted - single test)\n")

ggsave("results/LR_planktovsMC.svg", p_taxon_env, width = 4, height = 4, device = "svg")
```

# 16. HAB-genus edges at a data-driven 75th-percentile cutoff

Threshold is recomputed from **each lake's own** `|asso|` distribution (75th
percentile), not a fixed round number, consistent with the earlier
diagnostic in Section 5 showing these are symmetrized MB coefficients, not
Pearson/partial correlations with a conventional "moderate" cutoff.

```{r hab-75pct}
# FIXED (Rmd review, redundancy #3): renamed from `hab_edges_all` (which
# collided with the Section 6 object of the same name) to
# hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes. FIXED (redundancy #4): computed directly from
# lake_results$net$edgelist1 in memory, not re-read from the CSVs just
# written in Section 15.
hab_edges_75pct_list <- lapply(names(lake_results), function(code) {

  edges <- lake_results[[code]]$net$edgelist1
  cutoff <- quantile(abs(edges$asso), probs = 0.75)

  is_hab <- edges$v1 %in% HAB_TAXA | edges$v2 %in% HAB_TAXA
  passes <- abs(edges$asso) >= cutoff
  sub <- edges[is_hab & passes, ]
  if (nrow(sub) == 0) return(NULL)

  sub$HAB_genus <- ifelse(sub$v1 %in% HAB_TAXA, sub$v1, sub$v2)
  sub$Partner   <- ifelse(sub$v1 %in% HAB_TAXA, sub$v2, sub$v1)
  sub$Lake      <- code
  sub$cutoff_used <- round(cutoff, 3)

  sub[, c("Lake", "HAB_genus", "Partner", "asso", "cutoff_used")]
})

hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes <- do.call(rbind, hab_edges_75pct_list)
hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes$asso <- round(hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes$asso, 3)
hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes <- hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes[order(hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes$Lake,
                                                              hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes$HAB_genus), ]

write.csv(hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes, "results/hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("HAB-genus edges at 75th-percentile cutoff, by lake:\n")
print(table(hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes$Lake))
cat("\nCutoffs used per lake (|asso| >=):\n")
print(tapply(hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes$cutoff_used, hab_edges_75pct_all_lakes$Lake, unique))
```
